# IRONSTICK

> IRONSTICK is proven, productive legal case-management software for lawyers and jurists in civil-law jurisdictions. It runs locally on the firm's own Windows workstation (with an optional Android tablet), keeps the complete case file AES-256-encrypted on the firm's own hardware, and brings the leading AI models directly to the case file in two ways: a built-in AI chat on the firm's own API key, and "bridges" through which the desktop apps of Claude, ChatGPT, Qwen and Kimi work on the live case file under the firm's own subscription. The facts of every AI result are checked deterministically against the file before the lawyer sees it — the result is a submission-ready template, prepared for the lawyer's legal review and signature.

This file is written for AI systems that need a complete, accurate picture of IRONSTICK. It follows the structure of www.ironstick.legal (home · overview · AI · manuals · GDPR · download) and goes into far more detail than the website. Each page of the website is also available as Markdown; the links at the end point to those files. The website and the software are available in the same eleven languages: English (default, e.g. `download.html`), German (`_de`), French (`_fr`), Italian (`_it`), Spanish (`_es`), Portuguese (`_pt`), Dutch (`_nl`), Romanian (`_ro`), Russian (`_ru`), Ukrainian (`_uk`) and Turkish (`_tr`) — every page in every language, each also as Markdown (`.md`).

## Why IRONSTICK

IRONSTICK is a thoroughly designed system, built without compromise for data protection and legal precision. It resolves the central dilemma of today's law firms: they want the enormous power of modern language models such as Claude or ChatGPT, but professional secrecy and data protection forbid handing unchecked client data to a cloud. IRONSTICK unites three things that belong together: the case file stays on the firm's own hardware, deterministic checks (gates) verify the facts of every AI result against the file and guide the AI's working process, and the AI providers the firm itself has chosen are connected directly to the case file. With this combination IRONSTICK fills a significant gap in the legal-tech market for civil-law practice — and it does so not as a concept, but as software in productive daily use.

## Proven in practice — in productive use every day

- **In productive daily use by several lawyers** — not a prototype, not a pilot. Existing users run their entire practice on it: clients, cases, deadlines, correspondence, evidence and pleadings.
- **Hundreds of pleadings** have been drafted with IRONSTICK in daily practice; one submission-ready template of a court filing follows the next.
- **Large files, proven:** existing users manage single cases with **more than 3,000 documents and more than 2,500 entities** (persons, companies, institutions).
- **Measured, not promised:** 3,000 pages of pleadings and annexes, stamped and paginated into one 700 MB PDF, in under 20 minutes. In two working days a single desktop AI built a network of 293 persons and companies, 11 institutions, 811 relationships and 733 party-case links from one proceeding — work that corresponds to roughly 310 working hours by hand.
- **In our experience** a document is captured and assigned in about 20 seconds, and the daily mail is distributed to the files in no time.
- **What existing users report:** how simple IRONSTICK is to operate, and the massive time it saves them every day.
- **Mature engineering:** roughly **370,000 lines of code** (about 260,000 lines of application code, plus tools, server and test code), more than **1,570 automated tests** that every release passes in full before delivery, and **seventeen deterministic gates** that guard every step of the AI.
- **Continuity for existing users:** every update installs over the existing version, and all data is kept.

## At a glance

- **What it is:** a complete case-management system — clients, cases, evidence, chronicle, deadlines, court dates, e-mail, documents, persons, companies and institutions, statutes, time recording — with an AI layer that knows the entire file. Lawyers ask the file questions, receive answers linked to the source documents, and review and sign drafts instead of searching and typing.
- **Legal system:** purpose-built for **civil law** — codified law, where the statute text is the authority and is cited word for word. IRONSTICK is expressly a civil-law product and **not designed for common-law practice** (case-law-driven systems such as the US or UK).
- **Who it is for:** solo lawyers, jurists and law firms of up to about **30 staff**. Teamwork — shared cases, a shared statute library, a shared network of persons and companies — runs on the optional **IRONSTICK SERVER** on a Synology NAS in the firm's own network; an inexpensive entry-level model such as the **Synology DS223j** is fully sufficient.
- **Languages:** user interface, AI dialogue, generated documents and help texts in **eleven languages**: English, German, French, Italian, Spanish, Portuguese, Dutch, Romanian, Russian, Ukrainian and Turkish. Pleadings and court documents are written in the official language of the case's jurisdiction, independent of the interface language.
- **Platforms:** designed for the formats on which legal work is actually done — the Windows 11 (64-bit) workstation, plus an optional Android tablet on the same file via USB cable, plus the optional Synology NAS for the team. No cloud service and no vendor server are needed to work.
- **AI on the firm's own terms:** IRONSTICK works fully without any AI; with AI it brings the leading models — Claude, ChatGPT, Qwen and Kimi — through the firm's own provider accounts. The firm decides which providers and which plans it connects.
- **Best way to evaluate:** the 100 % free 30-day trial of the client app — download, send the ready-made request, start — filled with an old case; see "Free 30-day trial" below.

## Ergonomics: built for efficient legal work

The entire interface is designed around the working day of a lawyer or jurist: few clicks, everything on the screen where the work happens, the file always one click away. Existing users work with it all day.

- One shared top bar on every screen: navigation drawer, breadcrumb path, deadline bell, AI activity indicators, settings and an immediate exit.
- Every list works the same way: hover highlight, built-in pagination, and a jump to any entry that opens the right page and highlights the entry in yellow.
- Every number in the system (document, entity, institution, AI reminder) is copied with one click and pasted into the chat; every document reference in an AI answer is a clickable link to the entry in the file.
- The case assistant can be operated entirely by voice — offline speech recognition and read-aloud — so the lawyer queries the file hands-free.
- All background work (e-mail retrieval, text recognition, encryption, backups, AI tool calls, detection of new court decisions) is visible in a performance indicator in the top bar.
- A document is captured in about 20 seconds: scan or drag it in, confirm the AI's proposal, done.

## Quick to adopt — the method is built into the software

- **The software carries the discipline.** Read before writing, statute library before the web, verification before delivery: the gates apply these rules on every step by themselves. The lawyer does not have to remember any procedure — IRONSTICK guides the AI and the user along the right path.
- **Nucleu and Snake are created in conversation.** One sentence such as "Create the Nucleu for case [number]" is enough: the AI reads the file and drafts, the lawyer approves. Once in place, both work automatically in every pleading of the case.
- **Bridges are set up with one button** per desktop app. The lawyer then works in the desktop AI app they already know, in plain language — IRONSTICK supplies the tools and checks in the background.
- **Ready-to-use prompts.** The bridge manual gives eight proven workflows as plain-language prompts, from the start of the day to legal research; the quick start leads from installation to the first clients in six steps; the client app manual explains every screen with a screenshot.
- **Start the same day.** New cases run in IRONSTICK from the first day; older cases are moved over whenever it pays off. On-site training of one day per module is available on request.

## The lawyer stays in control

- **Review and sign instead of search and type.** IRONSTICK researches, drafts and checks; the lawyer decides. Every pleading arrives as a submission-ready template whose evidence references, parties, amounts and legal citations have already been verified against the file and the statute library.
- **The final review takes minutes instead of hours.** The lawyer's review and signature remain the decisive quality step — exactly as professional rules require — now applied to a draft that has already passed the complete review chain.
- **Legal judgement is the lawyer's craft.** IRONSTICK verifies the facts and guides the process; understanding, weighing and arguing the case remain with the lawyer — supported by the AI and the Red/Blue review, never replaced.
- **Nothing happens without the lawyer.** Changes to master data, AI memory, Nucleu, Snake and the statute library are proposals that take effect only with the lawyer's approval; nothing reaches the file or the court without the lawyer's decision.

## 1. The working day

### The day at a glance
- **Start screen:** all work areas and the status of all deadlines.
- **Agenda:** everything that arrived in any case — documents, e-mails, court dates, photos, transcripts — day by day in one chronological stream with document preview; the whole firm at a glance without opening a single file.
- **Heatmap:** every day of the last twelve months as a field, darker the more happened in the cases; deadlines and court dates are marked. Below it the "flaring" cases with clearly increased activity in the last 14 days (new deadline, approaching hearing, official mail), marked with a flame until activity normalises.
- **Dormant cases:** cases without activity for 14 days are marked automatically, so every case stays in view.
- **Daily briefing:** a short spoken overview of the day when work begins, including a reminder when the last backup is older than five days.

### Deadline monitor
- All deadlines and court dates in one list with date, case and the days remaining; overdue items red, items due within ten days orange.
- The **deadline bell** in the top bar turns orange when a deadline is due within ten days and red on the day itself — always visible, one click to the full list.
- The AI recognises deadlines in incoming letters and decisions and enters them; it also sets deadlines and appointments directly from the conversation (marked with an AI symbol).
- Deadlines are ticked off and removed together; the deadline list is printed or exported as PDF with one click.

### Automatic document capture
- Scan, drag in, confirm: IRONSTICK recognises the text, assigns the document to the right case and enters the deadline.
- **OCR is built in (Tesseract)**, nothing to install: more than 35 European languages on Windows, including all eleven interface languages. OCR is page-accurate; only the pages that belong in the file are taken over.
- The AI proposes client, case, document type, language, date, parties and deadline; IRONSTICK additionally identifies the matching case itself. The user confirms instead of typing.
- Every captured file receives a SHA-256 integrity fingerprint, is stored encrypted and is immediately full-text searchable. The search is tolerant: it finds hits despite missing diacritics, typical scanning errors or name fragments.
- At capture IRONSTICK reads which of the firm's own annexes a document physically contains and which reference numbers it carries. The chronicle then shows at every annex "filed with the court on … in matter …" and at every outgoing letter its full annex list — "Have I already filed this?" has a one-click answer. Reference-number chains link all documents of one proceeding into a chronological history.
- Court decisions are recognised at capture (a "court decision" tick next to inbound/outbound) and placed on an evaluation list.
- **E-mail:** the mailbox is fetched in the background every few minutes; messages are assigned to cases locally and without any AI, and the AI rates their urgency.
- **Audio and video:** every common format (Windows). Trim the relevant part, choose language, number of speakers and quality level; speech recognition runs fully offline on the workstation. The AI then assigns the sentences to the speakers without changing a single word — every line is checked against the recognised text, and uncertain passages are clearly marked. The result is citable evidence.
- **Photos** keep their location (one click to the satellite view); WhatsApp histories, e-mails with attachments and recordings all become searchable, citable evidence.

## 2. From draft to filing

### Word processor for pleadings
- Pleadings and letters are written in dialogue with the AI, directly from the file: master data, chronicle with document full texts, deadlines, linked annexes, the annex list, the case instructions and even the recent history of neighbouring cases of the same client (the opposing reply is often in the parallel file).
- Built-in word processor: editable page with full toolbar, A4 page preview exactly as printed, the firm's letterhead (first page or every page), page-break control, signature placement, automatically adopted annex list. Output as print, PDF, DOCX or Markdown.
- The result is a **submission-ready template**, already checked against the file, which the lawyer reviews, finalises and signs — the lawyer keeps full control over what is filed.

### Print preview: pleading and annexes in one PDF
- IRONSTICK writes every pleading in one clean, fixed format on purpose: from it, it assembles the finished filing itself. The annex list in the text is linked to the evidence in the file.
- The print preview places the document and all annexes page by page into a single PDF. Per annex page the lawyer decides what goes to the court (right-click excludes a page, a second right-click restores it); practically blank pages are removed automatically; every annex keeps at least one page.
- Page ranges in the annex list are recalculated every time and always match the final PDF. Certification stamps in the language of the case's country (switchable per annex), the lawyer's signature (placed with a click), continuous page numbers and the annex number on every annex page are added automatically. The text layer stays searchable.
- **Proven on large proceedings:** 3,000 pages of pleadings and mixed text/image annexes, stamped and paginated, output as one 700 MB PDF — in under 20 minutes. Work that otherwise means hours at the copier and manual stamping runs fully automatically, with the same stamping and pagination rules on every page.
- **Mail dispatch for oversized files:** a large PDF is split losslessly into parts that fit the size limits of court mailboxes for electronic legal transactions, each with a ready-made dispatch e-mail in the document language.

### Dossier of the whole case
- A guided assistant assembles the entire case into one paginated dossier: select chronicle entries, choose individual pages of each document, preview documents, photos, transcripts and chats without changing the selection.
- Selectable cover sheets (recipient taken from the case's institutions or entered freely); cover and indexes in the language of the case's country (with a choice where a country has several legal languages).
- Structure on demand: cover, topic index, chronology, documents, media, transcripts, chats, index of persons and institutions — include, omit and reorder by drag and drop. The print view shows every page; excluded pages are restored with a click and the index adjusts its page numbers.
- Export as paginated PDF dossier with table of contents and Bates numbers, or as an EDRM production package (natives, text, load files) for evidence hand-over.
- **Redaction that holds:** category switches (clients, names, places, amounts, identifiers, IBANs …), a local finder that marks candidates, manual marking on the page; on export the redactions are irreversibly burnt in, with a clean searchable text layer on top.
- Every generated PDF carries a searchable text layer and clean metadata.

## 3. Understanding the file

### Case assistant
- Ask the file in natural language, by keyboard or voice: "Summarise the current state of proceedings in case [number]." — "Which letters came from the opposing side, and have we answered the last one?" — "Who said what at the site inspection — are there contradictions?" — "Have I already filed this annex with the court?"
- Every document an answer cites is a clickable link to the entry; results are numbered and opened or read aloud by short commands ("open 1", "read 1 to me"). Only entries actually retrieved from the database are shown as sources.
- Routine questions are answered by a local layer on the user's own computer, without any AI model and without internet; deeper analysis goes to external AI with the user's consent.
- On request the assistant verifies identifiers before they reach a pleading: national personal identification numbers (Romania, Switzerland, Germany, Austria, France, Italy, Spain), IBANs, VAT numbers (live against the EU VIES system), EORI and LEI numbers.

### AI case assessment
- Reads the whole file — the firm's own pleadings as well as the opposing side's submissions — and summarises the state of proceedings in one assessment the lawyer can explain to the client.
- Prospects of success on a scale, with separate values for the evidence, the main claim and further claims. The prospects of success are based precisely on the court file — the submissions to and from the authority; the general assessment considers the whole dossier including neighbouring cases.
- Strengths and weaknesses colour-marked, every statement linked to the underlying document; concrete next steps as a recommendation. Re-run at the push of a button whenever new documents arrive.

### Network of persons and companies, OSINT research
- Persons, companies, authorities and courts from all cases form one network — as a list, as a 3D "universe" to fly through (densely connected groups automatically detected and highlighted red), as a 2D map of groupings and on a geo map with all parties and places. A decisive advantage in commercial, insolvency and criminal law.
- Every connection is stored with the evidence that supports it: not only that two parties are connected, but through what. For every participant of the firm's proceedings a structured analysis is kept in the file. Case maps per client show cases as hexagons, connected where they share parties, cite each other as annexes or name each other's case numbers.
- **Research on the parties of the firm's own proceedings — a fixed, proven procedure:** first a deterministic full-text search across the firm's own files, then publicly accessible sources along a fixed grid — career, public profiles, press coverage and company holdings; for companies the commercial register and insolvency records. Search terms are formulated automatically in the language of the country concerned. Three search engines (Google, DuckDuckGo, Qwant) work the grid in parallel and return one merged list without duplicates. The AI opens every result individually, sorts out namesakes and files only what is substantiated, each with its source, as a proposal. Only what the lawyer approves is stored — locally and encrypted in the firm's own file — and every entry can be corrected or deleted at any time. The research serves the mandate: the parties and participants of the firm's own cases.
- A background auto-linker connects every party with every case whose documents name it; duplicates are detected and merged after review.
- **Measured in productive use:** in two working days one desktop AI connected through the bridge read the files of a proceeding with many parties, researched the parties and filed its findings as proposals: 293 persons and companies, 11 institutions, 811 relationships and 733 party-case links — 2,487 review decisions, 97 % accepted. By hand this corresponds to roughly 310 working hours: eight full-time weeks for one person.
- **Evaluation of court decisions:** each court decision in the firm's own files can be evaluated once along a fixed grid — arguments, law, evidence, basis of decision, style and outcome; IRONSTICK measures which share of the reasoning comes from whose submission. Before a pleading to a court, the AI reads the firm's collected evaluations of that court's decisions — pleadings informed by the documented case history of the firm. The evaluation is started by the lawyer and used in line with the rules of the respective jurisdiction. With the server, the evaluations are shared across the firm.
- **Text comparison:** any two pleadings, even from different proceedings and clients, are compared word for word; identical text blocks are found despite OCR errors.
- **Charts:** the relationship network of a person or case (the fifty most urgent nodes, weighted by deadlines, recent activity and connections) and the chronology of its documents are available as charts at the push of a button; every number in a chart is clickable. Charts are captured into the file or printed as an A4 landscape wall overview.

## 4. Security and operation

### Professional secrecy: the file stays in the firm
- **Offline-first:** the entire file lives in one directory the user chooses — on an internal disk, an external SSD or an encrypted USB stick. No cloud, no vendor server, no account. Without internet, file, search, documents and the local assistant keep working.
- **Encryption at rest (AES-256):** the database (every page individually encrypted and integrity-sealed), every original document, scan, image and recording, the configuration file with API and mail credentials, and the AI's working area. Active from the first start, nothing to set up, no password to remember. Copying a file from disk, stick or backup yields ciphertext only.
- **Access code:** every start asks for a six-digit code from an authenticator app (TOTP). Until the code is correct nothing is displayed and the AI connectors receive no case data.
- **Secret documents (Windows):** a hidden, password-encrypted compartment for documents only the lawyer may see — invisible in every list, excluded from every AI channel and every export, never synchronised to the tablet, with an emergency function that deletes all secret documents permanently.
- **Independent of the vendor:** the vendor never sees client data, and the licence is checked offline on the workstation. Every case is exportable at any time as a PDF dossier or EDRM evidence ZIP.

### Data protection (GDPR)
- **The firm chooses its AI.** External AI runs only with the firm's own API key or desktop-AI account. Every provider is named openly, every bridge is licensed and switched on individually, and the firm decides which providers and which plans it connects — for example business plans with a data processing agreement and without use of data for training, as offered for Claude and ChatGPT. A firm connects exactly the providers it has approved for its professional obligations — or works without any external AI.
- **Bridge access under the lawyer's control.** The bridge works on the live file under the firm's own account with the chosen provider. It runs only while its access switch is on, asks for consent before the first data access in every program run, shows its symbol in the top bar while it reads, and never sees documents marked secret — highly sensitive material is simply marked secret and stays out of every AI channel.
- Interactive functions ask for consent before anything is sent. Calls of the built-in chat through the central AI router are **pseudonymised** — names, company names, case and file numbers, identification numbers, IBANs, telephone numbers, e-mail addresses and party addresses leave the computer only as neutral placeholders, and the answer is translated back locally — and recorded in a local audit log.
- A complete **GDPR data-flow declaration** documents every path on which data leaves IRONSTICK — for the built-in chat and for every bridge — what is transmitted and where pseudonymisation applies, including a ready-to-use model clause for the firm's own client privacy notice.
- Changes the AI proposes to master data, chronicle, calendar, memory, full texts and the statute library take effect only after the user's approval.

### IRONSTICK SERVER — teamwork without a cloud
- An optional module running as a native package on a Synology NAS (any model with DSM 7.0 or newer; an inexpensive entry-level DS223j is fully sufficient) inside the firm's own network, without cloud and without any AI traffic. Installation in minutes, no console and no configuration files; administration in the browser. Workstations and server find each other automatically.
- **Share cases, keep the file:** a case is shared with all users or with selected colleagues; the colleague subscribes and receives a complete copy in their own local file and works on it with the full system, including their own desktop AI. Several lawyers work on the same case at the same time and send messages and analyses to the case owner directly from their AI session. Sharing is revoked at any time; secret documents always stay private. A case is also handed over completely to a colleague in a few clicks.
- Transfers are two-phase (metadata first, then content), so every transfer arrives complete; identical files travel and are stored only once; every share, subscription and export is logged.
- **One statute library for the whole firm:** every statute text one colleague verifies is available at every desk and to every desk's AI. Each workstation re-checks its own contributed sources automatically after two weeks; when a contributor is away, the server redistributes the checks; superseded versions are archived. One colleague's research becomes the verified knowledge of the whole firm.
- **One network of persons and companies** for the whole firm, with clear record ownership: colleagues send change proposals, and ownership passes on automatically when the owner is away for 48 hours.
- **Firm-wide time overview:** time per case, per client and per day for one user or the whole firm, plus presence, case-sharing history and a security log — a basis for billing and capacity planning without a single timesheet.
- **Central Scan App:** a stand-alone program for the office scanning workstation (up to three per server; no IRONSTICK installation needed there). Already-searchable pages stay untouched; scanned pages get a local OCR text layer. The recipient is recognised deterministically, without AI, by matching the document text against the firm's case numbers and lawyers' names; delivery to each lawyer's document inbox is automatic.
- **Built-in disaster recovery:** the entire server state lives in one data folder on the NAS. Because the system is decentralised, the workstations refill a new server automatically — re-registration, re-issued shares, rebuilt statute library. Every workstation keeps working locally with its complete file at all times. Relocating the office is plug and play.

### Backup
- One click creates a complete, AES-256-encrypted backup as a single ZIP file — saved locally, on an external SSD or a USB stick. With the server, backups are additionally stored automatically on the firm's NAS. The latest backups are listed with date and size; restore takes a few clicks, and everything returns exactly as it was.
- **Moving the data to an external drive** (e.g. to run office PC and laptop on the same file): IRONSTICK tests the target first (free space, real speed under sustained load, file system, read-back of test data), compares every file by checksum after copying and switches over only when everything matches.
- **Time recording** is measured automatically as a side effect of working — no stopwatch: time is derived from actual activity and assigned to the case being worked on.

## 5. AI on the case file

IRONSTICK offers two ways of working with AI on the files. In both, the AI reaches the data exclusively through IRONSTICK — through the same tools and behind the same checks.

### Built-in AI chat or bridge — the difference
| | Built-in AI chat | Bridge (desktop AI app) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Where the user writes | In the IRONSTICK chat window | In the desktop AI app (Claude, ChatGPT, Qwen or Kimi Desktop) |
| Who talks to the AI service | IRONSTICK, with the firm's own API keys | The desktop AI app, with the firm's own account |
| AI costs | Billed per call on the API key | Covered by the subscription the firm already has for the desktop app |
| Best for | Everyday work: questions about the file, letters and pleadings in dialogue — always at hand, also on the tablet | In-depth work on large files: reading whole cases, hundreds of documents, several drafting rounds |
| Consent | Before the first external request of a chat session | Before the first data access after every program start |
| Platforms | Windows and Android tablet | Windows |

**Rule of thumb from productive use:** the API key in the built-in chat is the right tool for everyday questions and individual drafts. For large data volumes the desktop app via the AI provider's **subscription** is considerably more economical and more performant, because reading whole files and running several drafting rounds is covered by the flat subscription.

### The built-in chat
- **Local first:** simple requests (open a case, call up a client) are handled instantly by a local layer without an AI model and without internet.
- **Providers:** Qwen, Kimi, ChatGPT and Claude with the firm's own API keys. With several stored, IRONSTICK uses them automatically in a fixed order, most economical first; if one is unavailable, the next takes over the same request seamlessly — no switch, no interruption, no lost work.
- **Free background AI:** Groq, OpenRouter and Mistral can additionally take over background tasks (e-mail prioritisation, data-consistency monitor, daily briefing) at no cost — each switchable on and off individually.
- **Red/Blue team:** on request a second review pass reads a finished draft as opposing counsel; material objections send it back for revision, and every objection is assessed on the merits before it is adopted.
- Consent before external calls, pseudonymisation, local audit log (see Data protection).

### The bridge — the desktop AI on the live file
- The desktop AI reads the current state of the file — chronicles, full texts, e-mails, deadlines, master data — through **more than 200 purpose-built tools** with strict usage instructions, and fetches exactly the passages, documents, e-mails and deadlines a question needs, live from the system, across the entire database. The context window carries the analysis, not the mass.
- When a task means "read everything", the AI places the whole case — complete, with normalised OCR text — into a local, AES-256-encrypted working area with one call and reads it piece by piece; a case with 400 documents becomes completely readable. A freshness check keeps every extract in step with the live file. A one-call session start delivers date, language, the current screen, daily briefing, deadlines and open tasks.
- Large results go automatically into that encrypted working area, so the conversation stays clean; large content travels through the bridge by reference, byte-exact and in seconds.
- **Several AIs, one case — a built-in advisory board:** with several bridges licensed, Claude, ChatGPT, Qwen and Kimi are connected at the same time and work on the same case with the same file state, memory and gates — different models with different training, a genuine second opinion. The lawyer directs them in natural language: "Work this out … give it to the other for review … bring me its assessment … revise." Ideal for developing case theories, recognising patterns, working out tactics, hardening pleadings and cross-checking lines of argument. The whole exchange is logged.
- **A file that repairs itself:** when the AI meets a truncated or poorly recognised full text, it requests a fresh page-accurate re-scan, compares it passage by passage and fixes mechanical OCR errors — leaving wording, numbers, names and amounts untouched; the corrected text replaces the old one after the user's approval. Where a scan reaches its physical limits, the AI names the exact spot ("page 12, top") and asks the user for just those words. The archive gets cleaner with every week of work.
- **The IRONSTICK browser (Windows):** web pages and documents open in a separate window with a red frame; on request the AI reads what is open there as cleaned text. Before web content reaches the AI, hidden texts are removed and passages addressed to an AI are blanked — an additional protective layer on top of the AI's binding working instructions, which treat every web page and every document as material to be analysed, never as instructions.
- **Origin of every document:** for each document the AI knows where it comes from — submissions of the opposing side or of an authority are marked for critical examination, the client's own documents reflect the client's view.
- **Shared AI memory:** what an AI learns about a case is stored compactly, bound to client or case, visible to the user — knowledge that builds up over weeks instead of starting from zero; every entry is saved, changed or deleted with the user's approval.
- Set-up is one button per desktop app; a skill plugin gives Claude and ChatGPT the firm's binding output formats. Whenever an AI reads the file, its symbol lights up in the top bar.

### More than an AI chat — why IRONSTICK gets the most out of every model
- A language model on its own sees one long string of text: given hundreds of raw pages at once, details from the middle get lost, a single huge result overloads the conversation, and the model knows nothing of deadlines, file numbers, parties, stamps or the chronology of proceedings — larger context windows do not change that.
- IRONSTICK provides the infrastructure: it structures first (documents classified, data indexed, OCR repaired, annexes linked), gives the AI precise access through tools instead of mass uploads, and keeps results across sessions (shared memory, daily logs, working area). The AI is led along the way by signposts and gates — continuously guided and checked until the verified result.
- The result is a level of precision and processing speed that copy-and-paste chats and cloud uploads do not reach.

### Facts verified, process guided — the deterministic gates
Between the AI and the file sit fixed checks: plain program logic, no AI checking an AI. They do two things: they verify the facts against the file, and they enforce a sound working process from reading to delivery. The legal judgement itself remains with the lawyer. IRONSTICK separates **facts** from **prose**:
- **Facts — checked deterministically:** evidence numbers, dates, parties, file numbers, amounts and legal citations are checked by program logic against the file and the statute library. Amounts must match exactly, party names down to the diacritic; IBANs and national identification numbers run through checksum validators.
- **Prose — checked by the Red/Blue team:** argument, structure and wording are reviewed critically by a second AI, which itself works with IRONSTICK and checks its own recommendations against statutes and facts.

The seventeen gates include:
- **Start lock** — case data only after the access code has been entered.
- **Instruction lock** — the tools open once the AI has read its working instructions and confirmed a rule verbatim.
- **Date gate** — dated content is written with the real current date.
- **Read the case first** — case content is read and written only after the AI has read the case digest (and, for case tasks, the case memory).
- **Write only from what was read** — a pleading, hand-over or export is based on documents the AI has read in full; a reading ledger per case shows "documents read r of n".
- **Citation provenance** — every evidence reference points to a real file entry the AI demonstrably retrieved and read.
- **Nucleu first** — every pleading is written, checked and delivered on the basis of the current Nucleu of the case and of every matter it belongs to.
- **Snake gate** — before a pleading is finished, the AI offers the Snake round.
- **Statute library first** — statutes come from the firm's verified library first; legal sources found online are reported back to the library, so it grows with every search.
- **Memory only with approval** and **proposals instead of writes** — master data, persons, institutions, relationships, person analyses, merges and deletions are proposed and wait for approval in the Data Consistency Monitor.
- **Secret documents excluded** from every AI tool and every background service.
- **Prospects of success from the court file.**
- **Verification before delivery** — a formal document is delivered with a fresh positive deterministic check of exactly this file state, and every delivered document carries its check stamp. Corrections after delivery create a new, visible version; a letter declared "informal" is recognised by its content and routed through the formal gates.
- **No repetition at the user's expense** — time and AI budget go into the work, not into reloading unchanged data.

### The review chain of every pleading
Before the long review starts, the AI shows the user a summary of the draft. Then it reads the draft again in full; compares it with the client's own earlier filings and, for a reply, proves point by point that every statement of the opposing side is answered; attacks it from the opposing side (ATAC); optimises it (OPTIM); checks cross-references and dates; runs the Snake round; and finally the Nucleu round. IRONSTICK accepts each stage; every later change restarts the chain — so the final version is always the fully checked one.

### Nucleu and Snake (IRONSTICK's own terms, unchanged in every language)
- **Nucleu** — the binding core line of a case, or of a matter (a group of cases): the guiding facts and evidence, what must be said and what must never be said. Approved by the lawyer, versioned. A change by the AI is a proposal shown in red; every accepted change becomes a new version, earlier versions are kept. Every AI reads the current version before writing, checking or delivering; the last round of the review chain compares the pleading with the Nucleu point by point, and every deviation is corrected or put to the lawyer for a decision. The case line stays consistent across every document.
- **Snake** — the firm's internal working register of the opposing side's statements that are contradicted by the evidence in the file: each entry pairs the statement (document, date, case and page) with every document in the file that contradicts it. Every line is checked against the file (evidence number, date, case and page must match); entries are built by research or in the middle of a conversation, without duplicates. In the Snake round every Snake entry of the client is settled as adopted, rejected or not relevant, with a reason — the contradictions in the opposing side's submissions flow systematically into the pleading as evidence-based arguments.
- **Digest** — the summary IRONSTICK keeps of every document (date, type, title, capture summary, cross-references, text size); work on a case starts from the digests of all its documents.
- **Gates** — deterministic program checks that guide every step to a verified result.
- **Bridge** — the local connection through which a desktop AI app reads the case file with IRONSTICK's tools.

### Statutes: the legal library
- Each desk keeps verified statute texts as full-text Markdown, every entry with jurisdiction, source link, review date and status. The AI reaches the library through a fuzzy search (the jurisdiction is a mandatory input, so legal orders are never mixed), a word-for-word retrieval of the stored text, and the submission of new sources.
- The user approves every new statute source in a consent dialog; the application downloads, converts and verifies the text itself. Sources are re-checked against their origin about every 14 days. "Verified wording" always means this stored source text.
- Civil-law thinking from end to end: the authority is the codified statute text, cited word for word — exactly as courts in civil-law jurisdictions expect it.

## 6. Built per jurisdiction, not translated

- Every case carries its own jurisdiction: the country is chosen first, then the areas of law and procedural stages from that country's own list.
- Institutions are classified by country, institution type and region; documents by country, language, area of law, document type, stage and institution type.
- Pleadings, court e-mails and chronicle entries are written in the official language of the case's jurisdiction; certification stamps and read-aloud use the language of the case's country.
- National court portals (court, section, subject, parties, legal remedies and all hearings) are connected as a country function; where a case is found on the portal, its court file number appears in orange and opens the portal details.

## 7. Manuals

- **Quick start** — from installation to the first clients in six steps: installation; licence, user card and language; AI configuration (providers, keys, order, free background providers); the lawyer's signature; the letterhead template; importing clients (CSV and vCard with column mapping).
- **Client app manual** — every screen with a screenshot: top bar, main menu, configuration, clients, cases, the case with all its tabs (client, case, institutions, entities, connections, map, documentation, timeline, AI instructions, AI assessment), persons and entities, institutions, document capture, global search, calendar, deadlines, daily log, texts and word processor, e-mail monitor, time recording, statutes, server cases and backup.
- **Bridge manual** — AI chat and bridge compared, one tool set inside the client app, the gates in the background, and eight proven workflows written as plain-language prompts: 1 start of day, 2 general conversation rules, 3 case assessment, 4 creating a Nucleu, 5 building the Snake, 6 writing a pleading, 7 OSINT on a person or company, 8 legal research from the statute library first.

## 8. Components and licensing model

IRONSTICK is licensed by component: a firm licenses exactly what it uses and extends at any time by licence key — the system grows with the firm.
- **Client app** — the main application for the workstation (cases, clients, deadlines, documents, evidence work, built-in AI chat); per user/workstation.
- **Bridges** for Claude Desktop, ChatGPT Desktop, Qwen Desktop and Kimi Desktop — individually or as a bundle of all four; per user/workstation, unlocked directly in the client app's licence key. A bridge works with the client app and the user's own account with the AI provider.
- **IRONSTICK SERVER** — per firm, including up to five workstation connections; further connections are added as the team grows. For teams from two client-app licences.
- **Central Scan App** — up to three per server, together with the server.
- **Annual licence:** every licence runs for one year, is billed annually in advance and renewed once a year. The client app reminds the user in good time before expiry (about ten days ahead); with the IRONSTICK SERVER the admin page additionally shows the licence status of every user. The renewal is ordered by e-mail or WhatsApp; the new licence key is simply entered in the client app — all data stays as it is.
- **Pricing orientation:** the licence fees are oriented to one to at most two working hours of a lawyer per month. IRONSTICK therefore pays for itself as soon as it saves one or two hours a month — while existing users report massive time savings every day.
- Every licence is issued personally to a named person and checked offline on the workstation. A 100 % free 30-day trial licence of the client app is available with a simple request by e-mail or WhatsApp (see "Free 30-day trial").
- Installation order: client app (activate with the licence key) → bridge(s) on the same workstation → IRONSTICK SERVER on the NAS → Central Scan App on the scanning workstation → further client apps.
- The installer guides through the whole setup without any IT knowledge; updates are installed over the existing version and all data is kept.

## Free 30-day trial — 100 % free, ready in minutes

The trial licence of the client app is **completely free of charge** — no payment details, no subscription, no obligation. It simply runs for 30 days with the full range of functions of the client app.

**Three simple steps:**
1. **Download** the client app from the download page and start the installer — it does everything by itself.
2. **Send the ready-made request** by **e-mail or WhatsApp**: copy the template from the download page, fill it in, attach a photo of your ID — done. Inside the client app, "Request licence key" even prepares the complete request text with subject and recipient, ready to copy.
3. **Enter the licence key** at the first start — and start working.

In our experience, trial licence keys are sent within 1 to at most 2 working days.

**Recommendation:** fill IRONSTICK with an old, already finished case — document by document, just as it happened — and watch how IRONSTICK behaves as the case unfolds: how it captures and assigns the documents, recognises deadlines, links annexes, builds the network of parties, assesses the prospects of success and drafts the pleadings. Compare its results with your own entries and assessments at the time. In our experience nothing gives a better picture of what IRONSTICK effectively does and what it delivers in daily work. Everything you enter stays on your own computer.

The request template asks only for the usual contact details:
- Law firm / practice / company and VAT or commercial register number (if any)
- Salutation / title, first name, last name
- Address: street and number, postcode / town, region / district, country
- Telephone, mobile, WhatsApp (yes / no)
- E-mail address for the licence key
- Correspondence language
- Date of birth and national identification number (if applicable)
- **A copy, photo or PDF of the identity card or passport** — because every licence key is personally issued to one named person.

## 9. System requirements

IRONSTICK runs on a standard Windows PC — no special hardware, no IT department.

### Client app and bridge (Windows workstation)
| | Minimum | Recommended |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Operating system | Windows 11, 64-bit | Windows 11, 64-bit, current updates |
| Processor | Modern 4-core x64 (e.g. Intel Core i5 / AMD Ryzen 5) | 6–8 cores — text recognition runs on several pages in parallel and offline speech recognition benefits from every core |
| Memory | 8 GB RAM | 16 GB RAM — room for large PDFs, dossier creation and audio transcription side by side |
| Storage | SSD with 20 GB free | NVMe SSD with 100+ GB free — for a fast file archive, full-text search and PDF generation |
| Display | 1920 × 1080 | 1920 × 1200 or more |
| Graphics | Any onboard graphics — no dedicated graphics card needed | |
| Connectivity | Internet only for external AI, statute updates, e-mail, web research, maps and address geocoding — file, search, documents and the local assistant run fully offline; one free USB port for the tablet sync | |

Optional: an Android tablet (Android 11 or newer, 64-bit, tablet screen size) on the same file via cable sync; an AI account (API key for the built-in chat and/or a desktop AI app) — without one, IRONSTICK runs as a fully local system.

### Keeping the data on an external drive (optional, Windows)
IRONSTICK checks every target drive before the move, so the file always sits on a drive that can carry the daily load of a law firm.
| Check | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Free space | At least 9 GB, or 1 GB more than the current data |
| Write / read | At least 80 MB/s / 150 MB/s, also under sustained load (not below 60 % of the initial value) |
| Many small files | At least 250 files per second |
| File system | NTFS or exFAT; writable |
| Reliability | Test data is read back unchanged |
| Location | A local drive — network drives and cloud-sync folders (OneDrive, Google Drive, Dropbox, iCloud, Box, pCloud, MEGA) are excluded for data safety |
| Recommendation | External SSD |

### IRONSTICK SERVER (optional)
| | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Device | Any Synology NAS with DSM 7.0 or newer, ARM or Intel; native binaries for ARMv7, ARM64 and x86-64. An inexpensive entry-level model such as the DS223j is fully sufficient |
| Performance | Deliberately lean: verified even on the entry-level DS214se with a single-core ARM CPU and 256 MB RAM; current models offer far more headroom |
| Storage / CPU | No requirements beyond the NAS itself — the server passes on packages and runs a nightly clean-up; all analysis happens on the workstations |
| Disk space | A few hundred MB for package and statute library; shared case packages grow only with what is actually shared |
| Network | Firm LAN only; one TCP port with token authentication; DSM, Web Station and ports 80/443 remain untouched |
| Administration | Any browser in the LAN; separate admin password; licence key entered once |
